name: Port Hawkesbury
why: The case. The service town for the Point Tupper industrial area.

name: Richmond, Subd. A
why: The rural area of Richmond County that holds Point Tupper. The site and its tax base are here.
against: Large rural area; Point Tupper is a small part of it.

name: Inverness, Subd. C
why: The rural area around Port Hawkesbury. Workers may live here.
against: Inside the commuting area, so it cannot be a control.

name: Mulgrave
why: The town across the Strait.
against: Inside the commuting area, so it cannot be a control.

name: Antigonish
why: The next service town, about 55 km away.
against: University town: education is 20.4% of its labour force (2021 Census) against 9.4% in Port Hawkesbury. Not a comparison. May be inside the commuting area.

name: Guysborough (MD)
why: Across the Strait; own history of large projects that were announced and not built.
against: Possibly inside the commuting area; rural municipality, not a town.

name: Pictou
why: Harbour town beside a pulp mill that stands in another municipality (the same town-and-tax-base split).
against: The mill closed in 2020, which is its own shock.

name: Trenton
why: Small industrial town (rail-car and wind-tower plant, power station).
against: Part of the New Glasgow urban area; plant closures.

name: Stellarton
why: Small industrial town; head office of a large grocer.
against: Part of the New Glasgow urban area.

name: Westville
why: Small former coal town.
against: Part of the New Glasgow urban area; little industry now.

name: New Glasgow
why: Service town for an industrial county.

name: Amherst
why: Border service and manufacturing town.
against: About three times the size; no port.

name: Oxford
why: Small town with one main employer (food processing).

name: Bridgewater
why: Service town with a large tire plant.
against: Growing, and about three times the size; no mill closure.

name: Lunenburg
why: Port town with a fish-processing plant.

name: Queens (Liverpool)
why: Liverpool and the Brooklyn paper mill (closed 2012).
against: Liverpool has not been a separate municipality since 1996; the data covers all of Queens.

name: Shelburne
why: Small harbour town; shipyard and former base.

name: Lockeport
why: Very small fishing town.

name: Clark's Harbour
why: Very small fishing town.

name: Yarmouth
why: Port and ferry service town.
against: Fishery and ferry economy; twice the size.

name: Digby
why: Port and ferry town.

name: Middleton
why: Small inland service town.
against: No port and no heavy industry.

name: Dalhousie
why: Port town whose paper mill closed in 2008.
against: Lost its mill; merged into a larger municipality in 2023.

name: Campbellton
why: Regional service town on the Restigouche.
against: Twice the size; boundary change in 2023.

name: Atholville
why: Small town with an operating pulp mill.
against: Next to Campbellton; boundary change in 2023.

name: Belledune
why: Deep-water port, power station and a smelter (closed 2019) in a very small community: heavy capital, few residents.
against: Smelter closure; the workers live elsewhere.

name: Bathurst
why: Port and service town; mill and mine closures.

name: Miramichi
why: River port; pulp and paper mills closed in the 2000s.

name: Nackawic
why: Very small town built for an operating pulp mill.

name: St. Stephen
why: Border town with one large food manufacturer.

name: Saint Andrews
why: Small port town.

name: Sussex
why: Service town; the nearby potash mine closed in 2016.

name: Stephenville
why: Port and airport town; paper mill closed in 2005.
against: A wind-hydrogen project was announced there in 2022, a similar shock.

name: Grand Falls-Windsor
why: Paper mill closed in 2009.
against: Inland; about four times the size.

name: Clarenville
why: Service town where refinery and construction workers live; the plants stand in other municipalities.

name: Arnold's Cove
why: Small town beside an oil transshipment terminal and a refinery.

name: Come By Chance
why: Refinery site: heavy capital and very few residents.
against: About 200 people; shows the host-area side, not the town side.

name: Placentia
why: Port town near the Argentia site and the Long Harbour nickel plant.

name: Marystown
why: Shipyard and offshore fabrication town.

name: Channel-Port aux Basques
why: Ferry terminal town (as Port Hawkesbury was before the causeway).

name: Botwood
why: Port that exported paper until the mill inland closed in 2009.

name: Lewisporte
why: Port and service town.

name: Borden-Carleton
why: Former ferry town at a fixed link (the bridge opened in 1997), as the causeway was for the Strait.

name: Souris
why: Small port and ferry town with fish processing.
